rows.en:
Hello, everyone.
This meeting is finally drawing to a close, isn't it?
...Though it seems the seventh person isn't going to show up.
Well, setting that aside, let me begin my story.
My name is Tomoharu Hosoda.
I'm a second-year.{p}

{a}{f:|}, you know that restroom beside the gym that's off-limits now, right?
That filthy restroom nobody can use, yet it's been left there all this time.
That restroom is creepy, isn't it?
It's a waste of space, too.
They should either fix it up and use it, or just tear it down...
But you see, there's a reason they can't fix it and can't tear it down.
Something shows up there.
No matter how many purifications they perform, no matter how important a person they call in, that one place is hopeless.{p}

Even I don't want to go near that one place.
The aura drifting there is one of a kind; its quality is different from anywhere else.
How should I put it... It isn't human.{p}Hey, {a}{f:|}, what do you think it is?
Foxes
Tanuki
Fish
Bugs

You got it right.
{a}{f:|}, have you maybe been near that place yourself?
You seem like the same type of person as me, {a}{f:|}.
If you got a strange feeling there, that's only natural.
So, the story about bugs.
Did you already know this story?
It's the reason that restroom stopped being used.{p}

A long time ago, there was a male student.
Unfortunately, I don't know his name.
He hated bugs with a passion.
But there are two kinds of hating, you know.
The type who hates something so much they don't want to go near it, and the type who hates something so much they kill it.
Which one are you, {a}{f:|}?
The type who stays away from things you hate?{p}Or the type who kills them?
The type who stays away
The type who kills them

Whoa, you're crueler than you look.
I'd better make sure you never come to hate me, ahahaha...
Anyway, he was the same way.
When he saw a bug, instead of running away, he'd chase it down and stomp it to death.{p}

I guess he was cruel to begin with.
Even bugs have souls, but I doubt he ever gave that a moment's thought.{p}

Back then, that restroom beside the gym could still be used normally.
Apparently everyone used it a lot after P.E. class.
And he used that restroom too.
Then he happened to look over and, what do you know, a house centipede was crawling along the restroom wall.
"Gross!"
He kicked the wall with his shoe and squashed that house centipede flat.
It was after that that he made a discovery.
That restroom, you see, maybe because it was so humid, was always damp, and full of bugs.{p}

House centipedes, centipedes, slugs... if you looked carefully, there were dozens of bugs clinging to the floor and walls.
They say he spent most of his breaks in that restroom.
To kill bugs.
I think deep down he actually liked bugs.
Otherwise, I don't think he could have been so obsessed with them.
They say he practically lived in that restroom, as if something had possessed him.
It was a real obsession.
Apparently he used to say it all the time.{p}

"I'll kill every last bug in this world!"
Just like that.
Scary, isn't it?
I'm pretty fond of bugs, so it gives me the chills.{p}

Eventually, just killing bugs wasn't enough for him anymore.
Until then, he'd been satisfied just squashing them, but no matter how long he kept at it, the number of bugs never went down.
A day later, they'd gather in that restroom again from who knows where.
Well, of course they would.
There's no end of bugs, after all.
Him trying hard all by himself was a truly wasted effort.
So he thought about it.
Why did the bugs keep gathering?{p}

Bugs must have at least a little intelligence.
So if their companions were killed more cruelly, even bugs would get scared and stay away from here.
That's what he thought.
Quite an idea, isn't it?
If it were me, I'd think of some other way.
Like improving the ventilation, or keeping the restroom cleaner.
That would be more constructive, right?
But he was different.
And he carried it out, exactly as he'd planned.
Mostly for his own satisfaction.{p}

Tearing the legs and bodies off house centipedes and centipedes was a given.
He burned them with matches, poured strange liquids on them, stabbed them with thumbtacks and needles...
That restroom became something like a torture chamber for bugs.
Even his friends finally told him to stop, but he wouldn't listen to a word.
And he began to study even crueler ways of killing them.{p}

But the bugs didn't decrease one bit.
As if mocking his efforts, far from decreasing, they increased.
Like soldiers on a battlefield, climbing over the corpses of their fallen comrades to fight on.
He fought.
All alone, against the tiny bugs...{p}

"Let's try this method next."
He used cellophane tape to stick lots of bugs onto a big stone, about the size of a pickling stone.
So they couldn't move.
Then he'd slam it down onto the ground.
The bugs got sandwiched between the big stone and the concrete and squashed with a splat.
"How do you like that!
Did you see that, you lot?
That's how I'll kill bugs like you!
Hurry up and vanish from this world!"
He screamed it.
At an invisible enemy.{p}

But the bugs heard those words.
All kinds of bugs were clinging thickly to the restroom windows, listening intently to what he said.
And as if defying his words, the bugs multiplied more and more.
The way they multiplied wasn't normal.
The boys' restroom and the girls' restroom were both hit.{p}

You'd go to the restroom, and suddenly something would drip, drip down onto your hair from above.
You'd reach up to brush it off, and a giant centipede would coil around your fingers...
...You'd look up, and the ceiling would be covered with centipedes.
Or the water in the sinks would suddenly clog.
You'd look, and find the drain stuffed with dead bugs.
Things like that kept happening one after another.
The girls, apparently, made a huge fuss.
They stormed into the faculty room shouting that they'd never, ever use that restroom again.
And after that, hardly anyone used that restroom anymore.{p}

Of course, the boy who kept killing bugs got called in by the teachers too.
Apparently they chewed him out pretty badly.
Even so, he didn't learn his lesson at all.
He blamed the bugs, saying it was all their fault he got called in and scolded by the teachers.
He became even more determined to fight.
Once it gets that far, it's just abnormal, isn't it?
And then he resorted to one final measure.{p}What do you think he did?
He tried to find the bugs' boss
He tried to burn the restroom
I can't even imagine

"...Making a fool of me.
...I'll kill you!
...Every last one of you, I'll kill you all!"
He kept muttering things like that, over and over.
The school at night is very dark.
That restroom especially, since its fluorescent light was broken.
It was dim even in the daytime.
At night, you couldn't see a thing.
As he got close to the restroom, what do you know, there was a rustling sound.
A rustling, scraping sound, like things rubbing their bodies together, was coming from the restroom.
He held his breath and stepped into the restroom.
And then... it felt different under his feet than usual.{p}

There was no hard floor; the footing felt somehow unsteady and squishy.
When he pressed down and put his weight on his foot, it felt like stepping on a thick, fluffy carpet.{p}

Under the squishy stuff, he could feel the hard floor.
Without thinking, he shone the flashlight he was holding onto the floor.{p}

And the inside of the restroom was packed with every kind of bug imaginable.
And not just the floor, either, but the walls and the ceiling too.
It was less a restroom than the inside of the stomach of some unknown creature.
The floor, the walls, the ceiling, all of it was rustling and writhing as if it were alive itself.
For the first time, he felt afraid.
The bugs had been waiting, you see.
Waiting for him to come.{p}

He froze in place.
He felt as if he finally understood how terrifying the enemy he'd been trying to fight really was.
This was not an enemy he could ever fight.
The bugs are mighty...
That thought kept spinning around in his head.
But even though his mind was thinking that, his body wouldn't obey him.
He was so terrified that he acted on reflex.{p}

The person who found him the next day was left speechless.
The restroom reeked so much of gasoline that they went to look, and what do you know, there were huge numbers of dead bugs.{p}

Dead bugs were piled up like mountains on the floor, so there was nowhere to set foot.
Among them was one spot heaped especially high, like a little hill.
When they dug through it, a human face came out.
It was him.
He must have been terrified, because his hair had turned pure white, and he was all dried up like a mummy, as if all the life had drained out of his body.{p}

...What's wrong?
Are you feeling sick?
Your face has gone pale.
Should I stop the story here?{p}Or do you want to hear a little more?
I want you to stop
I'll hear a little more

Are you sure you're okay?
If you hate bugs, I can stop.
Are you really okay?
...All right, then I'll go on.{p}

After that incident, the restroom couldn't be used anymore.
Even when they cleared away the dead bugs, more bugs would gather from out of nowhere.
Besides, even if the bugs were gone, nobody would want to use a restroom like that, right?
These days hardly anyone knows this story, so it's fine, but back then everyone knew it.
Since nobody used it anymore, the only option left was to tear it down.
So they called in contractors to demolish the restroom, and... bad things happened.
Everyone involved in the work, you see, was tormented by nightmares.
Apparently it was a dream of having their bodies eaten by swarms of bugs.
If it were just one night, it would only be a bad dream, but it went on for days.
And it happened to every single person involved.
They all became afraid to sleep, and on top of that, couldn't stand the sight of bugs anymore.
So the work was called off.
And that restroom is still there today.
...Though it seems bugs don't show up in that restroom anymore these days.{p}

Well, that story is just a rumor passed down at this school.
Nobody actually saw it, and nobody checked it, either.
I'm just repeating what I heard from an upperclassman, word for word.
So it's not very credible, is it?{p}Would you believe that story, if it were you?
I believe it
I don't believe it
Maybe it could be true

Right?
If you don't see it with your own eyes, you can't believe a gross story like that.
I was the same way.
I was just like you, {a}{f:|}.{p}

...Actually, a friend of mine fell victim to it.
All because he used that restroom.
That friend's name was Keiichi Tsuda.
Tsuda didn't use that restroom for fun or anything.
He knew the stories about that restroom, more or less.
And he hated bugs, too.
In Tsuda's case, though, hating bugs meant he was the type to run away.
Far from killing bugs, he was the type who couldn't even go near them.
So there's no way he'd ever go to a restroom with rumors like that by choice.{p}

Even so, one day, after P.E. class, he suddenly had to go to the restroom.
It was better than wetting himself, so he went, reluctantly.{p}

...Luckily, there were no bugs.
Even so, the walls were covered in dark, blackish stains.
He knew right away that they were stains from squashed bugs.
So he tried his hardest not to look, not to look, and hurried to do his business.
He held his breath, shut his eyes, and thought only about getting out of the restroom.
And when he was done, he made a dash for it.{p}

Outside the restroom was a whole different world.
Then, just as he stretched out big and took a deep breath...{p}

"Aagh!"
Tsuda couldn't help screaming.
He looked, and there was a huge spider on his shoulder.
It was a big joro spider with a yellow-and-black striped abdomen.
Thinking it must have hitched a ride when he went to the restroom, he jumped up and shook his whole body.{p}

The jorogumo fell from his shoulder and scuttled away just like that.
Even so, Tsuda's heart was still pounding.
And he got worried that there might be other bugs on him besides that one.
But he couldn't search.
He was too scared.
That's how people who hate bugs are.
What if there's one on my back? What if there's one on my head?
Even while thinking that, he was too scared to check.
His body froze up, you see.
That's how much he hated bugs, and how scared of them he was.
And he swore he would never go near that restroom again.{p}

Then one day, a few days later.
It was during lunch break.{p}

I'd finished my lunch and gone up to the roof, and over in a corner, Tsuda was eating his lunch alone.
Tsuda was a light eater.
He always ate like the food tasted awful.
As for me, mealtime is when I'm happiest.
Tsuda was the exact opposite.
He always seemed to be forcing himself to eat because he had to.{p}

But get this.
That time, he was wolfing it down like a different person.
He was shoveling the contents of his lunch box into his mouth at a furious pace.
I waved and walked over to him.
"Hey, Tsuda!"
Tsuda only gave me a quick glance and didn't stop his chopsticks for a second.
He had to be eating something really tasty.
Thinking maybe I'd ask him for a bite too, I went closer, and...
I nearly threw up what I'd just eaten.{p}

Then, once he'd polished off a whole lunch box of flies, he wiped his mouth, looking very satisfied, and let out a sigh.
And then he looked at me.
"What's wrong, Hosoda?"
He said it as if he couldn't understand why I was standing there frozen.
Then he closed the lid of his lunch box, walked right past me, and went downstairs.{p}

I couldn't move for a while.
Even now, I can't forget the way he looked at me.
That wasn't the way you look at a friend.
No, it was nothing that mild.
That wasn't the way you look at a human being.
It was the way you look at food.
After that, I decided to keep away from Tsuda.
I mean, wouldn't you?
Even if it was just an illusion I saw, I didn't want to be looked at with those eyes.
But bad luck comes looking for you anyway.
During chemistry class, I was told to go and fetch some lab equipment.
The teacher picked me by name.{p}

"Hosoda, Tsuda, sorry, but could you go to the prep room and bring back the equipment?"
Hey, {a}{f:|}, what would you do?{p}Would you want to be alone with a guy who eats flies like they're delicious?
Go with him
Ask the teacher to pick someone else

I begged the teacher desperately.
I said I had a headache, a stomachache, whatever, and escaped to the nurse's office.
The teacher looked annoyed, but let me go.
No matter what, I didn't want to be alone with Tsuda.
But that was a mistake.{p}

There was no one in the nurse's office.
I was lying in bed by myself.
Then, after a while, I heard a noise over by the door.
Thinking the school nurse had come back, I looked over, and...{p}

Tsuda was standing there.
With that look in his eyes, like he was looking at food.
Without thinking, I murmured,
"...Tsuda."
Tsuda was smiling.
It was the smile of someone who had cornered his prey.
"...Hosoda, that's mean of you.
Do you hate me or something?
I've had that feeling these past few days."
Then he slowly came toward the bed.{p}

I couldn't move.
I was paralyzed.
I was so terrified that my whole body had seized up.
Just like a bug caught in a spider's web.
Tsuda seemed to know that too.
He wasn't in any hurry; he came closer slowly, ever so slowly.
"...Hosoda, you're nice and fat, you look delicious.
What kind of things do you eat to get like that?"
As he said that, he suddenly climbed up onto my bed.
He straddled me and drooled happily.{p}

I wanted to cry.
And I knew for certain this was the end.
Fangs had grown in Tsuda's mouth.
And strands were trailing from his gaping mouth.
Not drool, but real silk.
He was just like a spider.
He's going to eat me!
...Just as I thought that, my body moved, just a little.
It was truly a godsend.
Somehow I managed to twist my body just a little.{p}

"Aagh!"
It happened all of a sudden.
All I did was twist my body, but out of nowhere Tsuda started writhing in agony.
He tumbled off the bed, clutching his head and kicking his legs wildly.
My paralysis broke, you see.
Without thinking, I threw off the blanket that was on top of me.
And then...
Under my body, a joro spider had been crushed flat.
Its abdomen had burst, and a thick, gooey fluid was oozing out.
And Tsuda stopped moving right there.
I ran.
I left Tsuda lying there.{p}

When I came to, I was in a hospital bed.
I'd been saved.
And I savored the joy of being alive with my whole body.
"Hosoda."
Suddenly, I heard someone calling my name.
Wondering who it was, I turned toward the voice, and...{p}

It was Tsuda.
Tsuda was lying in the bed next to mine.
The shock I felt then, I can't even put into words.
My heart really nearly stopped.{p}What do you think I did then?
